title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: A student types "book the laser cutter tomorrow 3 pm". Your Python handler always runs the same three steps in this order: (1) one model call turns the text into a machine and a time, (2) plain code calls the calendar API and inserts the booking, (3) one model call writes the confirmation message. Which description is right?

options.text: An agent, because the model reads free text and writes the reply
A workflow, because your code, not the model, picks each next step
An agent, because the program calls an external API as a tool
A workflow, because it makes only two calls and agents make many

items.stem: Your code is: `while True: reply = call_model(messages); if reply.has_no_tool_request: break; result = run_tool(reply.tool, reply.args); messages.append(result)`. You wrote the `while` and the `break` yourself. Is this system a workflow or an agent? Answer with one word.

A fixed workflow answers each availability question with exactly 2 model calls. An agent version of the same assistant averages 6 model calls per question (5 tool requests, then the final answer). Assume every model call costs $0.003 and there are 800 questions per day. How much more does the agent version cost per day, in dollars?

A design reviewer asks that no booking is inserted before the calendar has been checked for a conflict, and the team must be able to rely on that for every request. Which design should the team choose?

options.text: An agent whose system prompt says to check the calendar first
A workflow where the model decides whether to run the check
A workflow that inserts the booking, then checks and cancels on conflict
A workflow where code calls insert only after the check passes

items.stem: For an API's support tickets, every ticket first needs the same two steps: classify its urgency, then look up the customer's plan in the database. Only "unknown error" tickets then need open-ended digging through logs, where the number of steps varies a lot. Which design is best for a small model budget?

options.text: One agent loop for the whole ticket, so every step stays flexible
A fixed workflow throughout, with the log search repeated five times
Fixed code for the two set steps, then an agent loop for the logs
A coordinator agent that hands each step to its own sub-agent

items.stem: Which of these tasks most needs an agent, because the next step depends on what the previous result turned up?

options.text: A failing booking test: read files, run tests, edit and re-run until it passes
A nightly job that loops over tomorrow's bookings and has a model draft each reminder
A translator that loops over every manual page and has a model translate it to Spanish
A form handler that sends each submitted question to a model and stores the answer
